transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's getting to be a real problem. Right now, my kitchen table is completely covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I'll sit down there, and I just don't know which thing to do first... and I end up just sitting there looking at it until the whole day is gone.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing or organizing your tasks your whole life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Well, honestly, it's been my whole life. Even back when I was a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books and my homework... and I always needed constant reminders to just finish my seatwork before I could go outside to play. So, yes, it's always been this way, it just feels like it's getting harder to manage now.
Do you find that you spend a lot of your time worrying excessively about everyday events or potential problems in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like my husband's health or if we have enough for groceries, but it doesn't take over my day. It's not the worrying that keeps me stuck at the kitchen table, it's just... I can't figure out where to start. So no, I wouldn't say I worry excessively.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in doing the things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy the things I've always liked doing. I love going to my church group and spending time at the senior center. I still want to do all of it. The problem isn't that I don't want to do things or that I don't enjoy them... it's just that I can't seem to get myself organized enough to actually get out the door or finish the projects I start. But the interest is definitely still there.
Do you often feel like you have an inner restlessness, or do you find it difficult to sit still for long periods of time?

Yes, I do. I mean, even when I’m really trying to just sit politely in a meeting or a group, I can't quite seem to do it. I'll catch myself rubbing my hands together, or tapping my foot... or I'll be clicking my pen and just shifting around in my chair. I end up moving around so much that people actually look over at me. So, yes, sitting still for very long is definitely hard for me.
Do you find that you often interrupt others when they are speaking or find it difficult to wait your turn in conversations or group settings?

No, I don't think so. I'm pretty good about waiting my turn to speak, especially at the senior center or church. I might lose track of what they're saying sometimes, but I don't jump in and interrupt them. I just wait until they're finished.
When you are working on tasks or projects, do you find that you often make careless mistakes because you aren't paying close attention to the details?

No, not really. I mean, I might lose focus and just not finish what I'm doing, but I don't think I make a lot of careless mistakes when I'm actually working on something. If I'm knitting or doing a puzzle, I usually do it right... it just takes me forever, or I get sidetracked and walk away from it. But the details themselves are usually fine.
